## Author

**Yibing Xia** — University of Toronto, JSC370 (Data Science II), 2026.

## Course context

JSC370 is a project-based data science course at UofT; this final project is the capstone deliverable. It builds on a midterm submission that scoped the same dataset with linear-model baselines on raw count outcomes; the final project adds a per-capita rate target, tree-based models, lag features, and a COVID-period inferential specification with an explicit year-by-post-2020 interaction.

## Data sources

Five tables, all from Statistics Canada's [bulk CSV API](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/type/data) (no API key required):

- [17-10-0149-01 — Components of population change by CMA, 2021 boundaries](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1710014901) — provides the two outcomes (`net_interprovincial`, `net_intraprovincial`) plus `intl_inmigration` and `natural_increase_rate`.
- [17-10-0148-01 — Population estimates, July 1, by CMA](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1710014801) — total population and age-share breakdown (`share_25_44`, `share_65plus`).
- [34-10-0133-01 — CMHC average rents for areas with population ≥ 10,000](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=3410013301) — `avg_rent` and derived `rent_deviation`.
- [14-10-0020-01 — Unemployment, participation, and employment rate by educational attainment](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1410002001) — provincial `unemployment_rate` and `participation_rate`.
- [27-10-0273-02 — Expenditures on research and development by performing sector](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=2710027302) — provincial `rd_provincial`.

No API key or authentication is required for any of these tables; the pipeline downloads the bulk-CSV ZIP for each table and caches it locally under `data/raw/` (gitignored). Re-running the pipeline reuses the cache.

## Reproducibility

The entire analysis is reproducible from a clean clone by rendering two notebooks:

```bash
# From the project directory
cd JSC370_2026/project/canada_migration

# 1. Rebuild outputs/tables/* and outputs/figures/*
quarto render migration_analysis.qmd

# 2. Rebuild the written report as HTML
quarto render final.qmd

# 3. Build this website (outputs to site/_site/)
cd site && quarto render
```

The first render pulls ~2.3 GB of StatCan data on first run (components of population change is a large file); subsequent renders read from `data/raw/` in seconds. Processed data (`data/processed/panel_cma.csv`, `train.csv`, `test.csv`) and every figure/table are regenerated deterministically.

## Acknowledgements

Instructor and TA feedback on the midterm directly shaped the final scope: the primary-vs-secondary goal split, the rate target switch, the explicit random-split rejection as leakage, and the `year:post_covid` interaction for the inferential specification.
